extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the functorial group-theoretic constructions, rigidity properties, and categorical notions (radial/multiradial environments, mono-theta environments, cyclotomes, cuspidalizations) appearing in Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory II. Focus is on producing the indicated groups, subquotients, cohomology classes, and categorical structures from given input data Π, X_k, or MΘ_*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Π¨Y(Π) (open subgroup corresponding to tempered covering ¨Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are functorial group-theoretic algorithms for constructing from Π the open subgroup Π¨Y(Π) ⊆ Π corresponding to the tempered covering “¨Y”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted reference: [EtTh], Corollary 2.18, (i); see discussion preceding [EtTh], Definition 2.7. The algorithm is functorial in Π and produces the subgroup realizing the tempered covering ¨Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of subquotient (l · ΔΘ)(Π)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are functorial group-theoretic algorithms for constructing from Π a certain subquotient (l · ΔΘ)(Π) of Π (the subquotient “(l · ΔΘ)(MΘ)” of Definition 1.1, (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted reference: [EtTh]; the subquotient appears together with Π¨Y(Π) in the constructions leading to cohomology classes θ(Π).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of θ(Π) in H^1(Π¨Y(Π), (l · ΔΘ)(Π))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm Π → θ(Π) ⊆ H^1(Π¨Y(Π), (l · ΔΘ)(Π)) producing the set θ(Π) of μ_l-multiples of the reciprocal of the '(l · Z × μ2)-orbit ¨ηΘ,l·Z×μ2 of an l-th root of the étale theta function of standard type'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the constant multiple rigidity property of [EtTh], Corollary 2.19, (iii). θ(Π) consists of μ_l-multiples (μ_l = group of l-th roots of unity) of the specified reciprocal; see [EtTh], Definition 2.7 for precise notion of étale theta functions of standard type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and construction of ∞θ(Π)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ∞θ(Π) ⊆ lim_{→ J} H^1(Π¨Y(Π)|J, (l · ΔΘ)(Π)) as the subset of direct limit elements for which some positive integer multiple coincides, up to torsion, with an element of θ(Π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J ranges over finite-index open subgroups of Π; notation '|J' denotes the fibre product ×_Π_J. The phrase 'some positive integer multiple' may be interpreted multiplicatively as a power if modules are written multiplicatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of inversion and pointed inversion automorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist inversion automorphisms ι_X, ι_¨Y of the relevant curves/coverings (order two automorphisms) and the associated decomposition group D_{μ−} determined up to conjugacy; pairs (ι_¨Y, (μ−)¨Y) or equivalently (ι_¨Y mod Inn, D_{μ−}) are referred to as pointed inversion automorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses uniqueness of torsion points μ− of order 2 and lifting properties; refer to [EtTh], Remark 2.6.1 and the discussion of lifting ι_X to ι_¨Y determined up to l·Z-conjugacy and composition by Gal(¨Y_k/Y_k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of étale theta functions of standard type (restriction condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'étale theta function of standard type' is defined by the condition that its restriction to the decomposition group D_{μ−} is a 2l-th root of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See [EtTh], Definition 1.9, (ii); [EtTh], Definition 2.7. This is the local restriction criterion characterizing 'standard type'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of projective systems of mono-theta environments (discrete rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A projective system of mono-theta environments In MΘ_* = {... → MΘ_M → ... } is uniquely determined, up to isomorphism, by X_k (the discrete rigidity property of [EtTh], Corollary 2.19, (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index M varies multiplicatively over N≥1 and each MΘ_M is a mod M mono-theta environment isomorphic to the model determined by X_k. See Remark 1.5.1 for the role of discrete rigidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition morphisms of the projective system are isomorphisms and lift
rubrics_metrics.description: The transition morphisms of the resulting projective system of topological groups {... → Π_X(MΘ_M) → ... } are all isomorphisms; moreover any isomorphism of topological groups Π_X(MΘ_{M'}) → Π_X(MΘ_M) (for M dividing M') lifts to a morphism of mono-theta environments MΘ_{M'} → MΘ_M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus one identifies the various Π_X(MΘ_M) via these isomorphisms and denote the limit group Π_X(MΘ_*). References: Definition 1.1, (i); [EtTh], Corollary 2.18, (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of open subgroup Π¨Y(MΘ_*) and associated subquotient (l·ΔΘ)(MΘ_*)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the projective limit notation one obtains an open subgroup Π¨Y(MΘ_*) of Π_X(MΘ_*) and a subquotient (l · ΔΘ)(MΘ_*), analogous to the Π¨Y(Π) and (l·ΔΘ)(Π) constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Proposition 1.5 and connections to Proposition 1.4; these structures are available in the projective (environment) setting and are identified compatibly across levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism and exterior cyclotome Π_μ(MΘ_*)
rubrics_metrics.description: The projective system of exterior cyclotomes {... → Π_μ(MΘ_M) → ... } determines a projective limit exterior cyclotome Π_μ(MΘ_*) equipped with a uniquely determined cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l · ΔΘ)(MΘ_*) ∼→ Π_μ(MΘ_*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtained by applying the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Definition 1.1, (ii) to members of the projective system; see Proposition 1.5, (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm producing θ_env(MΘ_*)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm MΘ_* → θ_env(MΘ_*) ⊆ H^1(Π¨Y(MΘ_*), Π_μ(MΘ_*)) constructing an exterior cyclotome version of θ(Π) (θ_env transported via cyclotomic rigidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may think of 'env' as abbreviation for '[mono-theta] environment'. Also define ∞θ_env(MΘ_*) similarly as direct limit subset where some positive integer multiple equals an element of θ_env.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Kummer-theoretic construction when arising from a tempered Frobenioid
rubrics_metrics.description: If MΘ_* arises from a tempered Frobenioid C then the construction of θ_env(MΘ_*) is compatible with the Kummer-theoretic construction of the étale theta function (via Galois actions on roots of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function) and with the Kummer theory of the base-field-theoretic hull C_bs-fld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Propositions 1.2, 1.3, and citations [FrdII], Theorem 2.4; [AbsTopIII], Proposition 3.2, (ii). This signals compatibility between environment-level θ and classical Kummer classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological Kummer-class injection and identification of torsion subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural Π_X(MΘ_*)-equivariant injection Π_μ(MΘ_*) ⊗ Q/Z → lim_{→ J} H^1(Π¨Y(MΘ_*)|J, Π_μ(MΘ_*)) whose image equals the torsion subgroup of the codomain; the torsion subgroup is identified with the torsion of H^1(J_G, Π_μ(MΘ_*)) and follows from injectivity of the Kummer map for MLF's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses the fact that Π_μ(MΘ_*) is torsion-free and standard Kummer theory statements; see Remark 1.5.2 and references [AbsTopIII], etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cores: construction of Π_C(Π) with augmentation to Π/Δ
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a functorial group-theoretic algorithm Π → Π_C(Π) producing a topological group Π_C(Π) equipped with an augmentation (surjection) Π_C(Π) → Π/Δ, with kernel Δ_C(Π), that contains Π as an open subgroup in a fashion compatible with respective surjections to Π/Δ; when Π = Π^tp_X the inclusion identifies with Π^tp_X ⊆ Π^tp_{Ck}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted reference: [AbsTopII], Corollary 3.3, (i). The construction effectively computes various centralizers of images of open subgroups of Π/Δ in outer automorphism groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic cuspidalizations Π_UN(Π) with surjection to Π
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer N there is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm Π → Π_UN(Π) giving a topological group Π_UN(Π) with a surjection Π_UN(Π) → Π (so the augmentation to Π/Δ factors through), and when Π = Π^tp_X this surjection identifies with the elliptic cuspidalization arising from an open immersion determined by N-torsion of a once-punctured elliptic curve forming a double cover of C_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted reference: [AbsTopII], Corollary 3.3, (iii). The construction amounts to computing outer isomorphisms between subquotients of Δ compatible with outer actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability to chains of elementary operations (Belyi cuspidalizations etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous functorial group-theoretic algorithms can be obtained for more general constructions involving 'chains of elementary operations' (e.g., Belyi cuspidalizations) as discussed in [AbsTopI], §4 and [AbsTopII], Corollary 3.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 1.6.1 explains that cores and elliptic cuspidalizations are instances; the general machinery computes centralizers and compatible outer isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of radial data, coric data, and the radial functor Φ: R → C
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'type of mathematical data' may be formalized as a category R (objects = collections of radial data, morphisms = isomorphisms); coric data similarly form C; a functorial algorithm radial gives Φ: R → C whose input is radial data and output is coric data, assumed essentially surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This axiomatizes the notion of a radial environment. Collections {Φ_i: R_i → C}_i∈I are considered when multiple labeled copies share the same codomain C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial vs uniradial environments (fullness criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A radial environment (R, C, Φ) is multiradial if Φ is full; otherwise it is uniradial. Multiradiality may be thought of as the condition that the radial algorithm does not result in any loss of rigidity (i.e., application does not collapse isomorphism data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Φ is not full, objects of R may lose rigidity when mapped to C; multiradiality is interpreted as 'no loss of rigidity' and is tied to the ability to lift isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological multiradialization construction
rubrics_metrics.description: When any two collections of radial data are isomorphic one can define a tautological multiradialization (R_mtz, C, Φ_mtz) whose objects are triples (R, C, α) with α: Φ(R) ∼→ C a full poly-isomorphism; this constructs a multiradial environment by 'forgetting the uniradiality' minimally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction yields a natural functor R → R_mtz given by R ↦ (R, Φ(R), Φ(R) ∼→ Φ(R)). See Example 1.7, (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality equivalent to switch functor invariance in R ×_C R
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiradiality implies that the switching functor sw: R×_C R → R×_C R (which swaps factors) preserves isomorphism classes of objects; equivalently every object (R1,R2,α) is isomorphic to (R1,R1,id:Φ(R1)∼→Φ(R1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a categorical criterion for multiradiality in terms of the fiber product category R×_C R; see Example 1.7, (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notion of multiradially/uniradially/corically defined Ψ_R between radial environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Ψ_R: R → R† with commutative diagram over coric categories, Ψ_R is multiradially defined (resp. uniradially defined) if it arises from functorial algorithms preserving multiradiality (resp. uniradiality); Ψ_R is corically defined if it factors as Ξ_R ◦ Φ for some functor Ξ_R: C → R† arising from a functorial algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corically defined maps are special cases of multiradial ones when R = C and Φ = id_R; see Example 1.7, (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality enables parallel transport and lifting of gluing isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ψ_R is multiradially defined, one may simultaneously execute the corresponding functorial algorithm relative to collections of radial input data indexed by I in a way compatible with identifications of coric portions; multiradiality allows lifting gluing isomorphisms in C to R and then applying Ψ_R to obtain corresponding gluing isomorphisms of output data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Ψ_R were uniradial this lifting is not possible a priori because outputs of Ψ_R may depend on additional rigidity in R not visible in C. See Example 1.7, (v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fullness as the condition to lift isomorphisms (connection/parallel transport analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fullness of Φ allows lifting isomorphisms in C to isomorphisms in R (unique up to failure of faithfulness), enabling a 'parallel transport' operation between fibers of Φ; multiradial ≈ fibration with connection, uniradial ≈ fibration without connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is conceptual guidance (Remark 1.7.1) explaining why multiradiality matters for executing algorithms relative to families of input data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic example: radial environment (Π,G,α) with radial functor sending to G
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic radial environment is given by collections (Π, G, α) with Π a topological group isomorphic to Π^tp_X, G a topological group isomorphic to G_k, and a full poly-isomorphism α: Π/Δ ∼→ G; the radial algorithm sends (Π,G,α) ↦ G and is full and essentially surjective hence multiradial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the Figure 1.2 'different arithmetic holomorphic structures on a single coric G'; see Example 1.8, (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm (∗TM): Π → Π↦MTM(Π) producing MLF-Galois TM-pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm (∗TM) assigning to a topological group Π isomorphic to Π^tp_X an MLF-Galois TM-pair Π ↦ MTM(Π), whose underlying ind-topological monoid has a natural ring structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: [AbsTopIII], §3 and Proposition 3.2; the construction yields objects used in later radial environments and has a tautological isomorphism with (Π/Δ) O(...) restricted to Π.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm assigning O(...): G ↦ G ↦ O(G) and tautological isomorphism with MTM
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists an algorithm (∗(cid:2)) assigning to G ≅ G_k an MLF-Galois TM-pair G ↦ O(G), and a uniquely determined functorial tautological isomorphism (Π ↦ MTM(Π)) ∼→ (Π/Δ ↦ O(Π/Δ))|_Π identifying these constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underlies the radial environment in Example 1.8, (ii); see [AbsTopIII], Proposition 3.2, (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Γ-variants and ⨯-constructions producing M×TM(Π) and O×(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed subgroup Γ ⊆ Z_p^× one constructs Γ-variant functorial algorithms (∗×) that produce Π ↦ M×TM(Π) and G ↦ O×(G), with Γ acting naturally on outputs; this yields a multiradial environment where isomorphisms are compatible up to Γ-multiples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Example 1.8, (iii). The Γ-action is trivial on G and natural on O×(G). Isomorphisms of collections of radial data are defined modulo Γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic (∗μ) and co-cyclotomic (∗×μ) versions and Ism(G), Γ×μ
rubrics_metrics.description: By passing to torsion subgroups one obtains cyclotomic algorithms (∗μ) and co-cyclotomic (∗×μ) algorithms; define Ism(G) (G-isometries of O×μ(G)) and closed subgroups Γ×μ ⊆ Ism(−) to obtain analogous multiradial environments with Γ×μ-multiples controlling isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of Γ×μ include Ism(−) itself or the image of Z_p^× acting; see Example 1.8, (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shell version using I(G) ⊆ O×μ(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may equip G (cid:2) O×μ(G) with its associated log-shell I(G) ⊆ O×μ(G) (p^{-1} times the image of G-invariants of O×(G) in O×μ(G)) to obtain 'log-shell' versions of the multiradial environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace G (cid:2) O×μ(G) with the pair (G (cid:2) O×μ(G), I(G) ⊆ O×μ(G)) in the constructions of (v),(vi),(viii) to get log-shell variants. See Example 1.8, (ix).

rubrics_metrics.name: No coincidence of Aut(G)-induced automorphisms with Γ-elements having nontrivial Z_p^×-image
rubrics_metrics.description: In the contexts considered, no automorphism of O×μ(G) induced by an element of Aut(G) (e.g., inner automorphism by an element of G) coincides with an automorphism induced by an element of Γ that has nontrivial image in Z_p^×.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical non-coincidence observation is useful when analyzing identification/uniqueness issues in the various multiradial environments (Remark 1.8.1).
